executive_summary: As of June 30, 2026, the security intelligence unit has concluded an assessment of 20 identified vulnerabilities, categorized by a severity distribution of 0 Critical, 11 High, 8 Medium, and 1 Low. The organization’s current risk posture is characterized as Elevated, necessitated by the presence of multiple High-severity vulnerabilities that require immediate remediation to prevent potential unauthorized system access and remote code execution. CVE-2026-55698 (Lockfile Resolution Hijacking in pnpm) represents the most significant threat, as it permits the subversion of internal development pipelines, thereby threatening the integrity of the software supply chain. Consequently, the organization must adopt an aggressive defensive posture, prioritizing the immediate patching of these vulnerabilities to mitigate exposure to persistent threat actors. Leadership is advised to authorize immediate resource reallocation to support the rapid deployment of these critical security updates.
critical_actions: Immediate patching of CVE-2026-55698 in all pnpm-reliant build environments within 24 hours.
Remediate the arbitrary file write vulnerability in gonic (CVE-2026-49340) by enforcing strict input validation within 48 hours.
Implement the patch for CVE-2026-47424 to secure the OpenAM Groovy sandbox environment by close of business, July 1, 2026.
Apply vendor-issued patches for CVE-2026-55697 to mitigate pnpm repository configuration risks within 72 hours.
Address CVE-2026-55487 by validating manifest identities and updating build controls within 72 hours.
Conduct comprehensive auditing and remediation of remaining six High-severity findings by July 5, 2026.

cve_summary.finding_name: Lockfile Resolution Hijacking in pnpm
cve_summary.description: pnpm project environment lockfiles are vulnerable to resolution hijacking, allowing them to short-circuit the standard package-manager process and execute arbitrary bytes from a selected location.
cve_summary.poc: An attacker creates a malicious `pnpm-lock.yaml` file within a shared repository. When a user pulls the code and runs pnpm, the tool follows the forged instructions in the lockfile to download and execute arbitrary binaries instead of verified packages.

cve_summary.finding_name: Arbitrary File Write in gonic
cve_summary.description: The `createPlaylist` function in gonic allows authenticated users to write M3U content to an arbitrary path on the host system. This vulnerability facilitates unauthorized file creation or modification.
cve_summary.poc: An authenticated user submits a request to create a playlist with a crafted filename containing path traversal characters. The application writes the playlist data to an attacker-specified path on the host file system instead of the playlist folder.

cve_summary.finding_name: RCE via Groovy Sandbox Escape in OpenAM
cve_summary.description: OpenAM allows authenticated remote code execution via a Groovy sandbox escape vulnerability. An attacker with minimal privileges can execute arbitrary code on the server by bypassing script execution protections.
cve_summary.poc: An authenticated user sends a script to an endpoint that processes Groovy code. By leveraging specific reflection techniques that are incorrectly restricted in the current sandbox configuration, the attacker escapes the environment to run arbitrary system commands.

cve_summary.finding_name: Remote Command Execution via pnpm Config
cve_summary.description: pnpm configuration allows repository-controlled dependencies to force the selection of an arbitrary pacquet native install engine, leading to potential command execution during the installation phase.
cve_summary.poc: A project repository contains a malicious configuration file that defines an alternative native install engine. When pnpm installs the project, it executes the specified engine binary, which the attacker has pointed to malicious code.

cve_summary.finding_name: Manifest Spoofing for Arbitrary Lifecycle Execution
cve_summary.description: pnpm manifest identity spoofing allows unauthorized packages to bypass `allowBuilds` security controls. This forces the execution of arbitrary lifecycle scripts, leading to code execution during dependency installation.
cve_summary.poc: An attacker publishes a package that spoofs its identity to match a trusted dependency in the manifest. pnpm incorrectly authorizes this package to run build scripts, allowing the attacker to execute arbitrary shell commands on the user's machine.

cve_summary.finding_name: Arbitrary File Write in pnpm Stage
cve_summary.description: The pnpm package manager suffers from an arbitrary file write vulnerability during the stage download process. Attackers can leverage malicious manifest names to perform directory traversal and overwrite files outside the target directory.
cve_summary.poc: A developer executes `pnpm install` on a malicious package. The package manifest includes a specially crafted name containing traversal sequences (../) that forces the pnpm installer to write files into sensitive system locations, potentially overwriting configuration files.

cve_summary.finding_name: IDOR in Subsonic API Playlist Access
cve_summary.description: The Subsonic API fails to properly authorize access to user-owned playlists. Any authenticated user can read or delete the playlists belonging to any other user via an Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) attack.
cve_summary.poc: An authenticated user identifies the numeric ID of a target playlist. By sending a crafted DELETE or GET request to the Subsonic API with the target's ID, the user bypasses authorization checks and modifies or accesses the remote playlist content.

cve_summary.finding_name: Path Traversal in gonic Playlist API
cve_summary.description: Gonic is vulnerable to path traversal within the playlist ID parameter. This allows an attacker to bypass ownership checks and manipulate file paths to read or delete arbitrary playlists.
cve_summary.poc: The attacker sends a request to the gonic API where the playlist ID is manipulated using traversal sequences like `../../`. The server resolves these paths outside the intended data directory, allowing the attacker to access files they do not own.

cve_summary.finding_name: OAuth Authorization Bypass via PKCE Challenge
cve_summary.description: OpenAM exhibits an authorization bypass flaw involving the handling of PKCE challenges in the OAuth flow. This allows an attacker to manipulate the authentication handshake, potentially resulting in unauthorized token issuance.
cve_summary.poc: An attacker initiates an OAuth flow and intercepts the authorization request. By crafting a malformed PKCE challenge-verifier pair, the attacker coerces the server into skipping verification steps, successfully obtaining an authorization code for an arbitrary user session.

cve_summary.finding_name: Host Header Injection in Nezha OAuth
cve_summary.description: Nezha Monitoring is vulnerable to Host Header Injection within its OAuth2 redirect flow. An attacker can influence the redirect URL, potentially redirecting users to a malicious site to harvest authorization codes.
cve_summary.poc: The attacker forces a user to click a crafted link containing a malicious `Host` header. The OAuth flow uses the injected host to generate the redirect URI, sending the user and the authorization code to an attacker-controlled server.

cve_summary.finding_name: Local File Deletion via pnpm Bin Name
cve_summary.description: pnpm allows for the deletion of `PNPM_HOME` during global remove operations due to reserved bin name mishandling. This leads to local denial of service by destroying the global package management directory.
cve_summary.poc: An attacker convinces a victim to globally install a malicious package. Upon running the uninstall command, the tool triggers a cleanup routine that mistakenly interprets a reserved bin name as an instruction to recursively remove the `PNPM_HOME` directory.

cve_summary.finding_name: WebSocket Resource Exhaustion in Nezha
cve_summary.description: Nezha Monitoring allows unbounded WebSocket streams, which can be exploited to exhaust server resources. This leads to a denial of service (DoS) by overloading memory or connection limits.
cve_summary.poc: An attacker opens a large number of concurrent WebSocket connections to the monitoring service without closing them. The server fails to enforce connection limits or timeouts, consuming resources until it is unable to handle legitimate monitoring traffic.

cve_summary.finding_name: DQL Injection in Dgraph GraphQL Queries
cve_summary.description: Dgraph is susceptible to DQL injection via the checkUserPassword GraphQL query endpoint. An attacker can manipulate backend queries to bypass security controls or extract sensitive data from the underlying database, leading to compromised confidentiality.
cve_summary.poc: An unauthenticated attacker sends a crafted GraphQL mutation containing malicious DQL syntax within the password field. The backend fails to sanitize this input, executing the injected query against the Dgraph store and returning unauthorized information to the attacker.

cve_summary.finding_name: OAuth Client Impersonation via JWKS Cache
cve_summary.description: OpenAM is vulnerable to client impersonation caused by improper validation of the JWKS resolver cache. An attacker can manipulate cached keys to sign illegitimate JWT tokens, effectively masquerading as a legitimate OAuth client.
cve_summary.poc: The attacker triggers the application to resolve a malicious JWKS endpoint containing a public key controlled by the attacker. By populating the cache, the attacker can then submit tokens signed by their corresponding private key, which OpenAM verifies as valid.

cve_summary.finding_name: Heap Overflow in ImageMagick SF3 Encoder
cve_summary.description: ImageMagick has a heap buffer overflow in the SF3 encoder during multi-frame image processing. Processing a specially crafted image can lead to memory corruption, potentially allowing arbitrary code execution.
cve_summary.poc: The attacker provides a specially crafted SF3 image file to an application utilizing ImageMagick. The library fails to perform adequate bound checking during the multi-frame write process, causing a heap overflow that crashes the service or enables code injection.

cve_summary.finding_name: Environment Secret Exfiltration via pnpm Config
cve_summary.description: A vulnerability in pnpm allows repository configuration to expand environment secrets into registry requests. This leads to the unintentional exposure of sensitive environment variables to third-party registries.
cve_summary.poc: An attacker creates a repository with a configuration file that uses environment variable interpolation in a registry URL. When pnpm runs in a CI/CD environment, it leaks the secret values in the HTTP headers or request body sent to the attacker-controlled registry.

cve_summary.finding_name: CSV Formula Injection in Statamic
cve_summary.description: Statamic is vulnerable to CSV formula injection in exported form submissions. Attackers can inject malicious spreadsheet formulas into input fields, which execute when a user opens the export in software like Excel.
cve_summary.poc: The attacker inputs a malicious formula (e.g., `=cmd|' /C calc'!A0`) into a public-facing form. When an administrator exports these submissions to CSV and opens the file in Excel, the embedded formula executes on the administrator's local machine.

cve_summary.finding_name: Memory Leak in ImageMagick Wand Parser
cve_summary.description: A memory leak exists in the ImageMagick Wand option parser when provided with invalid arguments. An attacker can trigger repeated memory allocation failures to cause denial of service.
cve_summary.poc: The attacker sends a high volume of requests to an ImageMagick-based web application with invalid command-line-style arguments. The parser leaks memory with every request, eventually exhausting system resources and causing the application to crash.

cve_summary.finding_name: SSRF via DNS Rebinding in Statamic
cve_summary.description: Statamic’s Glide component is vulnerable to Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) via DNS rebinding. Attackers can bypass internal network protections to perform unauthorized requests from the server.
cve_summary.poc: The attacker hosts a malicious domain that initially resolves to a safe IP but quickly switches to an internal IP (e.g., 127.0.0.1). By forcing Statamic's image processor to fetch from this domain, the attacker bypasses filters to interact with internal services.

cve_summary.finding_name: Unauthorized Preview Access in Statamic CMS
cve_summary.description: Statamic CMS has an authorization flaw allowing view-only users to access Live Preview content, which should be restricted to users with edit permissions. This results in unauthorized disclosure of unpublished sensitive content.
cve_summary.poc: A user with low-level access submits a crafted request for a draft page preview. The application fails to verify if the user has sufficient permissions to view the draft, exposing potentially sensitive pre-publication content to the user.
